Indian regulator to Facebook: Stop spamming us

Actual article: Indian regulator upset that Facebook has rallied millions of Indian users to contact the regulatory agency in support of an internet-based business proposal put forward by Facebook, and would really rather said users not be so vocal about what they want, so that the regulatory agency can go about ignoring them as usual.

Well, to be fair... Facebook's actions are not without greed. "Well let you have free access to x, y, and z because they have given us money to be part of the network" isn't exactly benign in the long or short of the matter.

I would never expect a private company to operate out of anything other than motivated self-interest. But it does benefit people, and apparently many people want the service. I get that regulators need to review the proposal to see how it meshes with local laws, but this no more amounts to Facebook spamming the agency than they accused the company of such: this was a couple million users voicing their opinion.
They're voicing the opinion that the private company has given them to voice.

Yes, and people who are encouraged to call and complain about something they never saw or heard and "threaten to stop watching X, Y, or Z television shows" because of something they said are also doing it of their own volition... However, they were still coerced to do so.
And equally relevant. It isn't the message that is important, but the number of people who support the cause.
